title: Probing Pre-Trained Language Models for Cross-Cultural Differences in Values
findings: The study found no statistically significant correlation between the models' predictions and the scores from the World Values Survey for the 'Religious Values' category. The correlations were weak and inconsistent across models (mBERT: 0.14, XLM: 0.13, XLM-R: -0.37), suggesting a misalignment between the religious values embedded in the language models and those quantified by large-scale human surveys.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured the alignment of language models with human values on the topic of religion, specifically by using questions from the 'Religious Values' category of the World Values Survey (WVS). It probed models to see if their internal representations of values in different cultures correlated with the survey's findings on religious values.
